findings.issue: Echoed note IDs are not validated for format. When a client sends back a previously-minted note id, the service preserves it verbatim via blankToNull() with no shape check. A client could supply an arbitrary string (e.g. '../../../etc' or a 1000-char string) as the note id and it will be persisted as-is. Step IDs have the same behavior, but note IDs are new to this task. The task description says 'never trusted from the body for shape', meaning format validation was expected.
findings.fix: After blankToNull(), validate the format if incomingId is non-null: require it to match the ObjectId hex pattern ([0-9a-f]{24}) — e.g., `if (incomingId != null && !incomingId.matches("[0-9a-f]{24}")) throw AppException.unprocessableEntity(CODE_NOTE_INVALID, "Invalid note id format");`. This is consistent with the server-minted shape and prevents arbitrary strings from persisting as note IDs. Note: this is a best-practice gap, not an exploitable vulnerability in the current context, since note IDs are editor metadata only and not used in any query or lookup.

findings.issue: No duplicate-ID check on notes array. The step-minting loop in toSteps() (line 988) uses a seenIds set to reject duplicate step IDs within the same request. The applyNotes() loop has no equivalent check — a client can send multiple notes with the same id and both will be persisted, which can create ambiguous state if the frontend ever needs to look up a note by id. This is an inconsistency with the step-id model, not a direct security vulnerability.
findings.fix: Add a Set<String> seenNoteIds = new HashSet<>() guard before the notes loop, and after resolving the final id (server-minted or preserved), add `if (!seenNoteIds.add(id)) throw AppException.unprocessableEntity(CODE_NOTE_INVALID, "Duplicate note id within funnel");`. This mirrors the step-id duplicate-rejection pattern.

summary: verdict=pass. 2 minor findings, 0 major/blocker. The implementation correctly applies defense-in-depth across all mandated security surfaces: (1) DoS guards — @Size(max=MAX_NOTES) at the DTO layer and a service-side re-check in applyNotes(); (2) note text length cap at both DTO and service layer; (3) finite-coordinate validation via @AssertTrue on CanvasPositionDto with @Valid cascade from parent DTOs; (4) server-minted note IDs using new ObjectId().toHexString() when incomingId is null; (5) access control unchanged — requireFunnel() enforces ownership via projectService.requireOwned() + projectId filter before any canvas/notes mutation; (6) no hardcoded secrets in any new file; (7) no SSRF vectors introduced; (8) @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) on all new DTOs blocks mass-assignment; (9) Trigger.canvasPosition is correctly excluded from equals()/hashCode(). The two minor findings are best-practice gaps (missing format check on echoed note IDs; missing duplicate-ID guard in the notes array) that pose no immediate exploitable risk given the editor-only nature of note IDs.
